summary: Show each checkpoint participant's revision advertised at its last daemon start

replay.detail: No replay or backfill. Status reads each participant's canonical latest own-origin daemon.started claim.

schema.detail: No storage or closed claim registry change. The existing daemon.started version string carries the stable machine version, bounded to 128 bytes.

rules.detail: Checkpoint build strings, proof-input identities, retention rules and agreement terms are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: Checkpoint JSON status adds an optional machine_version map for last-start advertisements, distinct from pending builds. Older responses decode with an empty map. Older or unstamped members publish bare versions and show not advertised. Revision and dirty marker now replicate to every member as fleet-internal metadata containing no secret; the existing startup string remains readable by older registries. Health version and fleet endpoint build are unchanged.

downtime.detail: No additional downtime beyond the ordinary daemon restart.

manual.detail: Each daemon publishes its startup version on every start, including restarts on the same revision. No repair or configuration conversion.

recovery.detail: Native Cargo, archive release and Nix stamp generators reject a machine identity longer than 128 bytes at build/evaluation time, before a release binary is produced. Startup retains the bound as a defensive guard against an externally supplied stamp. Correct invalid package/revision metadata before building. Rollback to a bare-version startup replaces the revision advertisement; status never guesses a revision from earlier claims.
